name: quit-content-focus
description: Cmd+Q after a click in the CONTENT pane (x=620) rather than the sidebar (x=140) - written as the control for quit-sidebar-focus. It did not control what it was meant to: its Escape never dismissed the palette and the click landed on the first-run search picker INSIDE the palette, so the quit went through the palette's pass-to-main-menu route and the pass said nothing about focus at all. It uses a reliable dismissal and gates, so it controls what it claims to.

actions.note: let the empty space render and the palette auto-open before trying to dismiss it
first dismiss attempt; unreliable on its own, hence the scrim click below
give the Escape time to land
second dismiss attempt - a press on the palette's scrim, clear of both the panel and the sidebar
let the palette close and key focus return to the browser window
THE VARIABLE: click the CONTENT pane. Measured off quit-sidebar-focus's captured frame - the content card spans roughly x 220-1010, y 40-700. This is the only difference from that scenario
let focus settle - same dwell as the sidebar case
evidence of where this click landed, to compare against the sidebar frame

assertions.label: palette-dismissed
assertions.note: Proves the palette really closed, so the content click landed on the page and not on the palette's picker - which is exactly what went wrong the first time.

assertions.desc: Cmd+Q quits after a click in the content pane (control for quit-sidebar-focus)

assertions.label: not-the-palette-route
assertions.pattern: Atrium: palette passing key-equivalent to main menu
assertions.note: Listed AFTER the quit assertion on purpose: the run log is pulled before assertions run, so a line Cmd+Q itself emits is only in the log that assert_quit re-pulls. Placed before it, this gate could never match - and a vlog_absent one would pass trivially, which is exactly the vacuous shape to avoid.
